title: GOD PUTS WORDS IN HIS MOUTH

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: God met with him, and Balaam said, "I have prepared seven altars, and on each altar I have offered a bull and a ram." The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak and give him this word." So he went back to him and found him standing beside his offering, with all the Moabite officials. - Num 23:4-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God does meet with Balaam, but not on Balaam's terms. Balaam mentions his seven altars and sacrifices, as if to remind God of all his effort. But God does not respond to the offerings. Instead, He simply puts His own word in Balaam's mouth and sends him back to deliver it.

This is a beautiful picture of God's sovereignty. Balaam had been hired to curse, but he could only speak what God gave him. The Lord took control of the very mouth that Balak had paid to pronounce a curse. The prophet became nothing more than a messenger of a word he could not choose.

We see how completely God rules over the situation. The plans of the powerful, the sacrifices, the schemes, all of it bends to the purpose of God. He can take the mouth meant for cursing and fill it with blessing. Nothing lies outside His control.

There is deep comfort here for God's people. When forces seem arrayed against you, remember that God can turn even the intentions of your opponents to serve His good purpose. In Christ, all things are working together for the good of those who love Him (Rom 8:28). The word that finally matters is always God's word.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you trust that God can overrule even the plans set against you?
2. How does God's control over Balaam's mouth comfort you?
3. Where do you need to rest in God's sovereign purpose today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Sovereign God, thank You that even the schemes of others bend to Your purpose. When I feel opposed, help me trust that You are working all things for my good in Christ. Amen.
